language.script_notes: Colombian Spanish as national; various Indigenous Amazonian languages spoken locally in the far south, rarely on formal signage.
false_friends: Venezuelan Llanos (the savanna continues across the border)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Minimal; the road network thins dramatically east of the Andes.
road_furniture.line_paint: As national where paved roads exist.
road_furniture.curb_style: Largely absent outside Villavicencio and a handful of towns; much of the deep Amazon (Leticia) is accessible only by river or air.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national on the limited road network.

architecture.roof_style: Simple pitched or flat roofs on ranch (hato) buildings in the Llanos; stilt or elevated construction near Amazon rivers given seasonal flooding.
architecture.wall_construction: Open cattle-ranch (hato) architecture defines the Llanos; simple wood-frame river settlements in the Amazon portion, similar to Peru's and Brazil's Amazon river towns.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted, practical tones reflecting the region's ranching/river-town character rather than dense urban development.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Cattle ranches (hatos) across the open Llanos grassland; simple river settlements in the Amazon; Leticia's unique tri-border river-port town (adjoining Peru and Brazil).

nature.vegetation: Vast treeless savanna grassland (the Llanos) dominates the north of this region — swamp grasses in low-lying flood-prone areas, long-stemmed grasses in drier areas; dense tropical Amazon rainforest takes over further south.
nature.terrain: Flat, low-elevation plains stretching from the eastern base of the Andes to the Orinoco river basin in the north, transitioning into the Amazon basin and dense rainforest in the south — together making up roughly half of Colombia's total area despite housing a small fraction of its population.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and seasonally flood-prone in the Llanos (wet/dry season savanna); consistently hot, humid and green in the Amazon rainforest further south — a stark, wide-open contrast to the mountainous Andean interior.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: 4WD vehicles and horses common on Llanos cattle ranches; river boats are the primary transport in the deep Amazon around Leticia.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Sparse; concentrated around Villavicencio and Leticia where roads/towns exist.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Among the sparsest coverage in Colombia — vast stretches of both the Llanos and the Amazon have no Street View coverage at all.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The same savanna grassland ecosystem continues seamlessly across the Colombia-Venezuela border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's yellow plates and narrow pole signage differ from Venezuela's; Venezuela's Street View coverage is notably older/sparser in recent years given the country's infrastructure challenges.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Amazon rainforest biome, similar river-town architecture around the shared tri-border region near Leticia
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Colombia's signage and plates are distinct from Brazil's Portuguese/Mercosur-style plates and Peru's road furniture; Leticia itself is a recognizable, relatively well-documented tri-border river port.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: This region is flat lowland — treeless savanna or dense rainforest; the Andean interior is cool and mountainous, and the coast is hot tropical coastline — all visually distinct.
